annotationRationale: The probability comes from counting equally likely sequences through exhaustive cases. Permutations order distinct transfers, combinations choose players, and multiset permutations handle the repeated transfers.
sourceMethod: Followed the official four-case count of balanced transfers. Added a cycle-decomposition justification for exhaustiveness and explained why repeated transfers require division by two factorials.

review.mathCheck: Each round has 12 equally likely directed transfers, and four starting coins make every four-round sequence feasible. Balanced transfers decompose into a four-cycle or two two-cycles. The disjoint cases contribute 144, 72, 36, and 288 sequences, giving 540/12^4=5/192, choice B.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of official solution 22 on page 9. All four patterns and counts agree; the added cycle argument explains exhaustiveness and the repeated-transfer denominator.
review.annotationCheck: The sample space, independence, repeated elements, and disjoint exhaustive cases are justified. Assessed and supporting counting concepts are appropriately distinguished.
